result.summary:
The Godot side of vehicle display v2 is done and committed (one commit, not pushed). tools/run_tests.sh passes: 235 unit tests and all 9 integration checks, none failing. The Xvfb sprite-flip check passes, and a full headless run of dev_testetappe with the test fixtures loaded finishes with no script errors.

1) SpriteDB reads grid_cols (cell = layer * angle count + angle), yaw_deg as a list or as a dictionary (the current manifest uses a dictionary), or derives it from the names (l2/l1/c/r1/r2 = -25/-12/0/12/25, l<n>/r<n> = -n/+n degrees). It also reads pivot, projection/camera/supersample and render "box" with parts/faces/lights. The old manifest still reads unchanged, and region() now follows the grid. New debug option --sprite-manifest=<path> merges another manifest over the real one; its aliases point real sets at fixtures and keep their tags. Sheets Godot has not imported are loaded straight from the PNG.

2) Traffic and police cars use the contract formula sin psi = (d_r * tan(h + psi_c) - x_r) / (d_r + L), limited to ±30°. h is the road chord from the car's rear to its front (exact for a constant curve). psi_c comes from each car's lateral speed, measured frame to frame by car id. The angle is smoothed per car (critically damped, 0.12 s) and only switches cell when the new cell is 0.3 steps closer. Unit tests show: the 16.5 m truck one lane over, 30 m ahead, gets -4.6° (the old formula gave 7.1°, i.e. the 12° cell); the drawn front sits within 0.5 px of the true perspective position across curves, lanes and lengths (old formula: up to hundreds of px off); a car on a constant curve with noise and uneven frame times changes cell 0 times (without smoothing and hysteresis, over 20 times).

3) Trucks/buses with render "box" (new BoxVehicle class):
- Visible faces are drawn as textured triangles in slices of at most 2 m that follow the road, so the box bends with the curve.
- Parts behind the camera's near plane are cut off, so a truck alongside stays visible while overtaking.
- Faces are drawn far to near and the vehicle is split at the scene slices, so it takes part in the normal back-to-front drawing (crests hide it, it sorts correctly against the player car).
- Fog, ambient light, night and tunnel lighting work as for sprites; tail/brake overlays, glows, a road shadow and anisotropic filtering are included.
- Unit tests confirm the drawn footprint is exactly the collision box.

4) Player car: perspective sets are anchored on the projected ground point of the car centre, scaled by distance_m / actual depth / supersample. The visible yaw is a smoothed sum of curve look-ahead (10 m), steering, lane-change lateral speed, understeer and a geometric view-angle term. Roll is up to ±2.5° from lateral acceleration. Brake lights, blinking and shake work as before. Old 5-angle ortho player sets still use the rear anchor. New settings: render.player_*, render.vehicle_*, render.box_*.

5) Visual check, using the new scenario tool tests/race/shoot_vehicles.gd (fixed frame rate, placed traffic, counts cell changes) and the fixtures from tests/fixtures/make_fixtures.py. Frame strips cover cars and trucks entering left and right curves, overtaking a box truck on straight and curved road (day and night), lane changes, the police car, the tunnel, the player in left/right curves and during lane changes, with fixtures and with current assets.

Draw cost (machine shared with Blender, load about 3.8): bench_render minima 4.35 ms before, 4.54 ms now with current assets, 4.80 ms with fixtures; medians 5.4–6.7 ms for all three. One box truck costs 0.08 ms at 200 m, 0.15 ms at 20–60 m and 0.35 ms right alongside.

docs/renn-modul.md is updated (§1, §2, §8, §11–§15).
contract_deviations: Player visible yaw (§3) has a fifth term besides the four listed ones: minus atan(lateral offset of the car from the camera axis / depth), weighted by render.player_view_gain (default 1). The perspective cell is rendered with the car straight in front of the camera; when the car is beside the axis (camera lag up to 1.1 m, road offset in curves) the cell is picked relative to the line of sight, which keeps the drawn rear and front within 1.5 px of the true perspective (unit test). Without it the rear is up to about 32 px off. Setting player_view_gain to 0 gives exactly the four contract components.

Road heading h in the §2 formula ('Straßenrichtung h an dieser Stelle') is taken as the chord of the road centre from the vehicle's rear to its front. That equals the heading at the vehicle's middle and is exact for a constant curve, so the drawn front lands within 0.5 px of the true position (unit test).

Box faces (§4): Godot canvas triangles map textures affinely (no perspective correction). Near the camera the slices are therefore shorter than 2 m (also at most 12 % of the depth, which 'höchstens 2 m' allows) and split into strips of constant depth until the texture error is about 1.5 px or less. Far away the slices are 2 m.

Box vehicles (§4) stay parallel to the road during lane changes (no own heading), so the drawn box always matches the TrafficSystem collision box. §4 defines no own heading for boxes; the box slides sideways.

yaw_deg is also accepted as a dictionary angle -> degrees (the format of the current manifest), in addition to the contract's list in angles order. This is a superset, kept for backward compatibility.
notes_for_lead: Merge with the sprite branch: test_sprite_db::test_box_parts_span_the_collision_box checks every box set in the real manifest. Each set's parts must span exactly object length_m x width_m around the centre (±5 cm), as §4 requires. A box set with mirrors or a shorter cab outside that rule will fail the test. The other SpriteDB tests use tests/fixtures/legacy/manifest.json and do not depend on how many angles the real sheets have.

Perspective player sheets must be rendered with the game camera (render.*: 3.4 m high, 9.0 m behind the car centre, fov 84°, horizon 0.45). The renderer warns when the camera in the manifest differs. 21 angles x 3 layers at supersample 2 hardly fit within 4096 px per side (my 486x320 cells at supersample 1.25 need 3402x2880 with grid_cols 7), so the pipeline needs tight crops or a supersample of about 1.5.

Box face atlases should pad the face rectangles with copied border pixels so mipmaps do not bleed between faces (make_fixtures.pack does this). The renderer also insets UVs by half a pixel and uses anisotropic filtering via a CanvasTexture.

Until the sprite branch is merged, the current assets work as before: 5-angle sets now pick their cell with the new formula and hysteresis; the old ortho player keeps its rear anchor. Old truck sprites are still drawn far too large when right beside the camera (inherent to ortho sprites, with a smaller angle than before); the box trucks fix this.

ARCHITECTURE.md is not my file and I did not edit it. Suggest adding pointers in §6 (new view keys: id per car, police id -2; player steer, lat_speed, push_speed, understeer, width; 'angle' now optional and no longer sent by the session) and in §12 (grid_cols, yaw_deg, pivot, projection, box). Both are fully documented in docs/renn-modul.md §8 and §15.

For the sprite developer, to check their sheets in game: xvfb-run -a -s "-screen 0 1280x720x24" godot --path . --rendering-driver opengl3 --audio-driver Dummy --fixed-fps 30 -s res://tests/race/shoot_vehicles.gd -- --scenario=overtake_curve --out=/tmp/x. Add --sprite-manifest=res://tests/fixtures/sprites/manifest.json to compare against the fixtures. Scenarios: curve_left, curve_right, overtake, overtake_curve, lane_change, player_left, player_right, player_lanes, police, tunnel. It also prints cell changes per car.

Frame strips, all under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-crossing-europe---a-racing-xperience/3a945943-d653-5a54-8279-676b9bc6f9e5/scratchpad/v2/race/: strip_ov_fx.png (overtaking a box truck), strip_ovc_q.png (overtaking in a left curve), strip_cr_fx2.png (truck and car entering a right curve), strip_plc_fx.png (player lane changes with yaw and roll), strip_overtake_night.png, strip_tunnel_fx.png, strip_overtake_cur.png (current assets).

tests_total 244 = 235 unit tests + 9 integration checks (check_session); the Xvfb sprite-flip check also passes. Performance was measured while the sprite render was loading the machine (load about 3.8 on 4 cores), so medians vary by about ±1 ms. The bench minima at the same five positions give the before/now comparison.
The relayed note that the repository is now public changed nothing: per the task, nothing was pushed or uploaded.

result.summary: Blender sprite pipeline v2 per docs/fahrzeug-darstellung.md. (1) Five new player cars (tools/blender/cesprites/player_cars.py on new carbody.py/cardetail.py/curves.py): smooth dense lofted bodies with spline profiles, creased shoulder line, flared arches, tumblehome greenhouse, protruding bumpers. All details are conformal patches ray-cast onto the body (glass with seals; tail lamps with frosted tinted lens, light housing, reflectors, LED light guides, brake segments; plates with text; diffusers/fins; exhausts; badges; seams; handles; headlights/grilles/intakes). Plus mirrors, rims (straight/twin/Y/turbine spokes, discs, coloured calipers), wing/spoilers/roof rails. Designs: kompakt = yellow hot hatch, black roof + spoiler; kombi = green estate, rails, L lamps; limousine = blue sedan, full-width light bar; sportwagen = red coupe, carbon wing, ring lamps, quad exhaust; gran_turismo = silver long-hood GT, ducktail, slim light strip, quad oval tips. Exact config length/width. Rendered with the game camera (9.0 m behind / 3.4 m up, horizontal, fov 84 deg -> focal 710.8 px, horizon 0.45), lens-shift cell, 21 yaws -20..20/2 deg about the centre, layers base/tail/brake (emission-only), anchor = projected ground point of the centre, camera block in the manifest. Showroom 768x480 3/4-front with steered wheels. (2) Traffic cars (26) and police (17): 17 ortho angles -24..24/3 deg, rear pivot, grid sheets, yaw_deg lists; traffic bodies smoothed with one subdivision level. (3) Trucks/buses: render "box" (truck: trailer z -8.25..5.35 + cab 5.75..8.25; bus: body). Face-on ortho renders of rear/left/right/top: rear 100 px/m, sides/top 80 px/m, exact integer rects, transparency between axles and around the cab. Tail/brake overlays, packed with 4 px edge padding; world-fixed lighting. (4) render_all.py: grid layout, perspective/box modes, manifest written after every set, CE_THREADS (default 3). New validator: 103 sets, 0 errors, 0 warnings. contact_sheet.py covers grids, all angles and box faces; reviewed sheets plus in-game simulations under scratchpad/v2/blender. (5) godot --import; 55 vehicle sheets (player/traffic/police) set to compress/mode=2, high_quality, mipmaps; re-imported as s3tc_bptc; .import files committed. PNG total 52.4 MB (budget ~60): player 17.4, traffic 19.4, police 11.5, props 3.2, showroom 0.9, ui 0.1. Estimated GPU memory with everything loaded is 305 MB: vehicles 263 MB as BPTC incl. mipmaps (~18-19 MB per player sheet, ~4.6 MB per police set), the rest 41.5 MB lossless; a race typically needs about 150 MB. tools/run_tests.sh passes (111 scripts compile, 211 unit tests, 9 integration checks OK). docs/sprites.md rewritten. Render time: traffic+police 47 min (2 threads), player+showroom+boxes 59 min (3 threads).
contract_deviations: Player sprites use supersample 1.9 (kompakt), 1.65 (kombi, limousine), 1.85 (sportwagen) and 1.7 (gran_turismo) instead of the 2.0 named in the task text. The contract only says 'z. B. 2.0' and requires sheets <= 4096 px per side. With the rear swinging out at +-20 deg about the centre, a long car covers 330-345 x 200-220 game px including its baked shadow, so 63 cells (21 angles x 3 layers) at 2.0 need 18-20 Mpx, more than the 16.8 Mpx a 4096x4096 sheet holds. render_all picks the largest factor <= 2.0 (0.05 steps) that fits. The actual value is in each manifest entry; cells are multiples of 4 px and the screen rectangle is exactly cell/supersample.

Box sets: besides the rear-face tail/brake overlays required by the task, lights.tail also lists the trailer/bus left and right faces (amber side marker lamps). Each entry has the same size and orientation as its face, which the contract format allows (a list of {part, face, rect}). The renderer must therefore accept light entries on side faces, not only on rear faces.
notes_for_lead: Angle names: player l20..l2, c, r2..r20; traffic and police l24..l3, c, r3..r24. yaw_deg is a list in the order of angles. Note that the player's l2/r2 now mean +-2 deg, not +-25 deg as before.

Perspective sets (player/*): image_width_m = cell width in metres in the plane of the car centre (cell.x * distance_m / (focal * supersample)), so cell.x/image_width_m stays the px/m at the car centre. anchor = projected ground point of the car centre (same for all 21 cells). Fields: projection 'perspective', pivot 'center', camera {height_m, distance_m, fov_deg, horizon_y_frac, screen [1280,720]}, supersample, grid_cols. Suggest drawing the player cell with mipmapped filtering (TEXTURE_FILTER_LINEAR_WITH_MIPMAPS), since it is scaled down by 1/supersample. The validator fails if config render.* no longer matches the manifest camera.

Box sets (traffic/truck_*, traffic/bus_*) have only file, render, object, tags, parts and lights, as in the contract example; there is no cell/angles/layers/anchor. Truck parts: trailer z [-8.25, 5.35] x +-1.275 y [0, 4.0] and cab z [5.75, 8.25] x +-1.25 y [0, 3.8]. Bus: body z [-6.4, 6.4] x +-1.275 y [0, 3.65]. Each part has faces rear/left/right/top; rects are [x, y, w, h] excluding a 4 px edge-replicated padding. The trailer faces include the tractor drive axle and tanks under the trailer nose; the cab faces are rendered without the trailer. Face lighting is fixed to the world (sun from above/behind, left and right sides equally lit), so the renderer may add orientation shading.

Unchanged in this worktree: SpriteDB/road_renderer still use the old column = angle, row = layer lookup, so grid sheets show wrong cells until the other half (SpriteDB v2) is merged. Tests pass regardless. For box sets the old code computes pixels_per_meter = 0 and simply skips drawing; there were no script errors.
Props, UI and the unchanged manifest entries were kept, not re-rendered. All set ids are preserved, and the traffic/police colours and countries are unchanged.
PNG total 52.4 MB. Estimated GPU memory if every sheet is loaded: 305 MB (BPTC with mipmaps for vehicles, lossless for props/showroom/UI). Per player car ~18-19 MB, per police set ~4.6 MB.

Review images (contact sheets, box faces, showroom, simulated in-game frames at 1x, day/brake/night): /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-crossing-europe---a-racing-xperience/3a945943-d653-5a54-8279-676b9bc6f9e5/scratchpad/v2/blender/ (contact_player.png, contact_traffic.png, contact_police.png, contact_boxes.png, showroom_final.png, ingame_*.png, lineup_vehicles.png).
ARCHITECTURE.md section 12 was not touched (not owned by me). It still describes the v1 format and could point to docs/fahrzeug-darstellung.md and docs/sprites.md.
The commit is on the worktree branch only (not pushed).
